WRITE (2–4 sentences): Explain your colors. Say which column you colored by
and why. If your first choice failed the color check, say what you changed:
fewer categories, grouping rare ones, or panels. Then look at your simulated
plot: can you still tell the categories apart?
My colors go from blue to green and are colored by the marital_status column. At first the color check failed so I grouped the separated and widowed values together as they had the smallest populations. Since there were now fewer categories the color check passed.

WRITE (3–4 sentences): Fixed or free? What does the reader gain, and what do
they lose? Which panels are small, and what is their n? Differences, not
causes.
Fixed scale because it allows for easier comparisons across the panels. They lose the ability to have a scale that best fits each panel but we gain the ability to more easily compare each panel.
